Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 51, verses 1–6:

This surah is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1–6} This is an oath by Allah, who is truthful in His speech, by these great creatures, in which Allah has placed such benefits and advantages as He has placed, to affirm that His promise is true, and that the religion, which is the Day of Recompense and reckoning for deeds, is certainly going to occur, and none can repel it. When the Great Truthful One informs of it, swears to it, and establishes the proofs and evidences for it, then why do the deniers deny it, and why do those who should work for it turn away from working for it?! {Wa-dh-dhariyat} (By the winds that scatter): these are the winds that scatter with their blowing, {dharwan} (scattering): with their gentleness, their subtlety, their strength and their agitation. {Fa-l-hamilati wiqran} (Then those that carry a heavy load): these are the clouds, which carry much water, by which Allah benefits the servants and the lands. {Fa-l-jariyati yusran} (Then those that glide with ease): these are the stars that move with ease and smoothness, by which the heavens are adorned, by which one is guided in the darknesses of land and sea, and by which one benefits from reflection. {Wa-l-muqassimati amran} (And those that distribute the affair): these are the angels who distribute and manage the affair by the permission of Allah; each one of them has been appointed by Allah to manage a matter of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter, not exceeding what has been limited for him, decreed for him and inscribed for him, nor falling short of it.

By the sky, full of its well-formed paths (ṭarā'iq ḥasana), which resemble the folds of sand and the ripples of pools when the breeze stirs them.

{10} Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Destroyed are the liars﴾; that is, may Allah curse those who lied about Allah, denied His signs, and engaged in falsehood in order to refute the truth with it, those who speak about Allah what they do not know.

{11} ﴿Who are in a flood of heedlessness﴾; that is, in a deep abyss of disbelief, ignorance and misguidance, ﴿heedless﴾.

{12} ﴿They ask: When is the Day of Judgment?﴾ in a manner of doubt and denial: ﴿When is the Day of Recompense [yawm al-din]?﴾ — they will be resurrected; that is, when will they be resurrected? Deeming it far-fetched!

{13–14} So do not ask about their condition and evil end! ﴿The Day they will be tormented over the Fire﴾; that is, they will be punished because of what they harbored of corruption, both inwardly and outwardly. And it will be said to them: ﴿Taste your trial﴾; that is, the punishment and the Fire, which is the result of the trial they were subjected to, which led them to disbelief and misguidance. ﴿This is﴾ the punishment you have come to, ﴿that which you used to seek to hasten﴾. So now, enjoy the various kinds of punishment and torment, the chains and shackles, the wrath and the calamity.

{15} Allah says, mentioning the reward of the God-fearing and the deeds by which they attained that recompense: ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing﴾; that is, those for whom piety was their emblem (sha'ar) and obedience to Allah their inner garment (dithar), ﴿will be in gardens﴾, containing every kind of tree and fruit, some having counterparts in this world and some having no counterpart, such as no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. ﴿And springs﴾, flowing freely, from which those gardens drink, and from which the servants of Allah drink, causing them to gush forth in abundance.

{16} ﴿Taking what their Lord has given them﴾. It may be that the meaning is that the people of Paradise have been given by their Master all their desires from every kind of bliss, and they take it, content with it, their eyes comforted by it and their souls delighted by it, seeking no substitute for it and desiring no change from it, for each one has attained of bliss what leaves no need for more. It may also be that this describes the God-fearing in this world, that they take what Allah has given them of commands and prohibitions; that is, they receive them with openness and an expanded breast, submitting to what Allah has commanded by carrying it out in the most perfect manner, and to what He has forbidden by refraining from it for Allah's sake in the most perfect manner, for what Allah has given them of commands and prohibitions is the finest of gifts, which deserves to be received with thanks to Allah for it and with submission.
The first meaning is more closely connected to the context of the speech, because it mentioned their description in this world and their deeds in His saying: ﴿Indeed, they were before that﴾, that is, before the time when they attained the bliss, ﴿doers of good﴾. This encompasses their good conduct in worshipping their Lord, by worshipping Him as if they see Him; for if they do not see Him, indeed He sees them. It also encompasses doing good to the servants of Allah by bestowing benefit and kindness of wealth, knowledge, standing, counsel, enjoining what is good, forbidding what is evil, or other forms of righteousness and paths of goodness. Indeed, this kind of good extends even to kind speech and gentle words, and to kindness toward slaves and animals, whether owned or not.

{17} Among the best kinds of good in worshipping the Creator is night prayer, which indicates sincerity and the harmony of heart and tongue. For this reason He said: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾; that is, the doers of good used to sleep only a little at night, and as for most of the night, they were devoutly obedient to their Lord, between prayer, recitation, remembrance, supplication, and humble entreaty.

{18} ﴿And in the hours before dawn﴾, which are just before the break of day, ﴿they would seek forgiveness﴾ from Allah, the Exalted. So they extended their prayer until the pre-dawn, then, at the close of their night standing, they sat seeking forgiveness from Allah the way a sinner seeks forgiveness for his sin. Seeking forgiveness in the pre-dawn hours has a virtue and a distinction not found in other times, as Allah the Exalted says in describing the people of faith and obedience: ﴿and those who seek forgiveness in the pre-dawn hours﴾.

{19} ﴿And in their wealth there was a right﴾, obligatory and recommended, ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾; that is, for the needy who ask people and for those who do not ask them.

The Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 51, verses 24–37:

{24} He, may He be exalted, says: {Has there reached you}; that is: Has it not come to you? {the story of Abraham's honored guests}: and their strange and wondrous news. They were the angels whom Allah sent to destroy the people of Lot, and He commanded them to pass by Abraham. They came to him in the form of guests.

{25} {When they entered upon him and said, "Peace." He said}, replying to them: {"Peace"}; that is: upon you. {"A people unknown."}; that is: you are a people unknown to me. So he wished that you would make yourselves known to me. He did not recognize them until after that.

{26} Thus he turned {to his family}; that is: he went quickly and secretly to bring their hospitality, {and brought a fattened calf}.

{27} {Then he placed it before them} and offered them the food, and {said, "Will you not eat?"}

{28} {So he felt apprehension of them}: when he saw that their hands did not reach to it. {They said, "Fear not."} and informed him of what they had come for, {and gave him good tidings of a learned boy}: and he was Isaac, peace be upon him.

{29} When the woman heard the good tidings, {she came forward} joyful and rejoicing {with an outcry}; that is: a cry, {and struck her face}: and this is of the same kind as what happens to women at joy and the like, of words and actions contrary to nature and custom. {And said, "An old woman, barren!"}; that is: how can I have a child when I am an old woman who has reached an age at which women do not bear children! And besides that, I am barren, my womb not being fit for childbearing at all. So there are two impediments, each of which is an impediment to having a child. And I have mentioned the third impediment in Surah Hud in her saying: {"And this is my husband, an old man. Indeed, this is an amazing thing!"}

{30} {They said, "Thus has said your Lord."}; that is: Allah, who decreed that and executed it; so there is no wonder in the power of Allah [the Exalted]. {Indeed, He is the Wise, the Knowing}; that is: who places things in their proper places, and whose knowledge encompasses everything. So submit to His judgment and thank Him for His blessing.

{31} {[Abraham] said, "What is your business, O messengers?"}; that is: Abraham, peace be upon him, said to them: What is your matter, O messengers? And what do you want? For he sensed that they were messengers sent by Allah for some important affair.

{32} {They said, "Indeed, we have been sent to a criminal people"}: and they are the people of Lot, who had committed crimes by associating others with Allah, by denying their messenger, and by committing the abomination that no one among the worlds had preceded them in.

{33–34} {To send down upon them stones of clay, marked from your Lord for the transgressors}; that is: each stone was marked with the name of its target, because they had been extravagant and exceeded the limit. So Abraham began to argue with them concerning the people of Lot, hoping that Allah would avert the punishment from them. Then it was said to him: {"O Abraham, give up this; indeed, the command of your Lord has come, and indeed, there is coming to them a punishment that cannot be turned back."}

{35–36} {So We brought out whoever was in it of the believers. But We did not find in it except one house of Muslims}: and they were the house of Lot, peace be upon him; except his wife, for she was among those who were destroyed.

{37} {And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment}: they take warning from it and know that Allah is severe in punishment, and that His messengers are truthful and their truthfulness is confirmed.

Section on mention of some of what this story contains of wisdom and rulings:
Among them: that among wisdom is Allah's relating to His servants the account of the righteous and the wicked, so that they may take heed from them and consider where their conditions led them.
Among them: the virtue of Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil), peace and blessings be upon him, in that Allah began his story with what indicates concern for its matter and attention to it.
Among them: the legitimacy of hospitality (diyafah), and that it is among the sunnah of Abraham the Friend, whom Allah commanded Muhammad and his community to follow in his creed; and Allah cited it in this place in a manner of praise and commendation.
Among them: that the guest is honored with all kinds of honor, by word and by deed; for Allah described Abraham's guests as honored, that is, Abraham honored them, and Allah described what he did for them of hospitality, in word and deed, and they are also honored with Allah [the Exalted].
Among them: that Abraham, peace be upon him, had a house that was a refuge for visitors and guests; for they entered upon him without seeking permission, and they followed the path of courtesy in initiating the greeting. So Abraham returned to them a greeting more complete and perfect than theirs, for he gave it in a nominal sentence (jumlah ismiyyah) indicating permanence and stability.
Among them: the legitimacy of getting to know one who comes to a person or who has some kind of connection with him, for there are many benefits in that.
Among them: the courtesy and gentleness of Abraham in speech; for he said: {"A people unknown"}, and he did not say: "I do not know you", and the difference between the two expressions is not hidden.
Among them: hastening to hospitality and being quick with it, for the best of goodness is that which is hastened; and for this Abraham hastened to bring the hospitality of his guests.
Among them: that a slaughtered animal that is present, which had been prepared for someone other than the present guest, if it is given to him, there is nothing in it of the least humiliation; rather that is of honor, as Abraham, peace be upon him, did, and Allah related that his guest were honored.
Among them: the abundant generosity with which Allah favored His friend Abraham, and that this was present with him and prepared in his house, not needing him to bring it from the market, from the neighbors, or otherwise.
Among them: that Abraham himself served his guests, and he is the Friend of the Most Merciful and the master of those who hosted guests.
Among them: that he brought it near to them in the place where they were, and did not put it in one place and tell them, "Please come to it," because this is easier and better.
Among them: the goodness of gently courting the guest in soft speech, especially when food is presented to him; for Abraham offered them in a gentle manner, saying: {"Will you not eat?"}, and did not say, "Eat!" or other words of which others are more fitting. Rather he used the particle of offering, saying: {"Will you not eat?"}. So one who follows him should use the good words that are suitable and fitting to the situation, such as saying to his guests: "Will you not eat?" or "Will you not do us the favor?" or "Will you honor us and do us good?" ... and the like.
Among them: that whoever fears someone for any reason, it is incumbent upon him to remove that fear from him and mention to him what reassures his heart and calms his inner distress, as the angels said to Abraham when he feared them: {"Fear not"}, and informed him of that joyful good tiding after the fear of them.
Among them: the intensity of the joy of Sarah, Abraham's wife, so much so that what happened from her of striking her face and her unusual outcry occurred.
Among them: what Allah honored Abraham and his wife Sarah with, of the good tidings of a learned boy.

{38} That is: {And in Musa (Moses)}: what Allah sent him with to Pharaoh and his chiefs of clear signs and manifest miracles is a sign for those who fear the painful punishment.

{55} {And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers}. Reminding is of two kinds. The first is reminding of what is known in its general outline through the natural disposition (fitrah) and the intellects, but whose details have not been recognized. God has created the intellects with a love of good and a preference for it, and a dislike of evil and a turning away from it, and His Law (shar') is in harmony with this. Thus every command and prohibition of the Law is a form of reminder, and the completion of the reminder is that one mentions what is in the commanded matter of good, beauty and benefits, and what is in the forbidden matter of harms. The second kind of reminder is reminding of what is already known to the believers, but which heedlessness and forgetfulness have overtaken, so they are reminded of it and it is repeated to them, so that it may settle firmly in their minds, they may awaken, act upon what they have recalled, and so that it may produce in them an energy and resolve that brings them benefit and elevation. God informed that the reminder benefits the believers, because the faith, fear (of God), turning back (to Him) and following the good pleasure of God that they possess necessitate that the reminder be effective in them and that admonition reach them in its proper place, as He, the Most High, said: {So remind, if the reminder benefits. As for one who has neither faith nor readiness to accept reminder, his reminding does not benefit him, like a salty land which the rain does not benefit at all. Such a category, even if every sign came to them, would not believe until they see the painful punishment.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 51, verses 56–58:

{56} This is the ultimate purpose for which Allah created the jinn and mankind, and for which He sent all the messengers, calling people to it. It is worship (ʿibadah), which includes knowing Him (maʿrifah), loving Him, turning to Him in repentance (inabah), directing oneself towards Him, and turning away from all else besides Him. This depends upon knowing Allah, the Exalted; for the perfection of worship depends upon knowledge of Allah. Indeed, the more the servant increases in knowledge of his Lord, the more perfect his worship becomes. This is the purpose for which Allah created the accountable beings; He did not create them out of any need He had for them.

{57} ﴿Tenfeeding nothing..." ﴾ Hmm — correction: ﴿I do not desire any provision from them, nor do I desire that they feed Me﴾. Exalted is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani), who is free of need of anyone in any respect. Rather, all creation is in need of Him in all their requirements and wants, the essential and otherwise.

{58} For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Provider (al-Razzaq)﴾; that is, the One of abundant provision, from whom no creature on the earth or in the heavens is without its provision from Allah, and He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage. ﴿Possessor of strength, the Firm﴾; that is, the One who has all strength and power, by which He brought into existence the great bodies, the lower and the upper, and by which He directs the apparent and the hidden, and whose will takes effect over all creatures. What Allah wills comes to be, and what He does not will does not come to be. No fugitive can escape Him, and no one can leave His dominion. Among His strength is that He delivers His provision to the entire world. And among His power and might is that He will resurrect the dead after they have been torn apart by decay, scattered by the winds, swallowed by birds and beasts, and dispersed and torn apart in desolate deserts and the depths of seas; not one of them escapes Him, and He knows what the earth diminishes of them. So glory be to the Strong, the Firm.
